classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a gradient, transfer it to the parallel opposite side, use equal directed coordinate changes to locate D, then apply the midpoint formula. The labelled diagram and explicit parts scaffold these routine linked procedures.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD on unticked Cartesian axes, with the three supplied coordinate labels and D labelled without coordinates. Source blue sides and red dots are rendered black as ordinary given geometry; the origin label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: A=(1,6), B=(5,10), C=(10,1); D is drawn at (6,-3) to preserve the parallelogram geometry but its coordinates are not printed. Edges AB, BC, CD, DA; positive-end axis arrows; no grid or ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: The diagram and supplied labels remain visible. D's coordinates and midpoint results appear only in answers.

answer.worked: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel, so $CD\parallel AB$. Hence $m_{CD}=m_{AB}=1$.

From $B$ to $A$, the horizontal change is $1-5=-4$ and the vertical change is $6-10=-4$. Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal and parallel, so the changes from $C$ to $D$ are also $-4$ and $-4$.
$$\begin{align*}x_D&=10-4=6\\y_D&=1-4=-3.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $D=(6,-3)$.
